findings.title: Extracting the Structure of Press Releases for Predicting Earnings Announcement Returns
findings.authors: Yuntao Wu, Ege Mert Akin, Charles Martineau, Vincent Grégoire, Andreas Veneris
findings.reason: FinBERT on 138k earnings press releases (2005-2023): press release soft info as predictive as earnings surprise for announcement returns. Direct extension of H163/H174 PEAD pipeline — adds press release body text as second NLP channel.

findings.title: PolySwarm: A Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework for Prediction Market Trading and Latency Arbitrage
findings.authors: Rajat M. Barot, Arjun S. Borkhatariya
findings.reason: 50-LLM swarm with Bayesian aggregation outperforms single-model and human superforecasters on Polymarket binary markets. Quarter-Kelly position sizing is principled. Directly applicable to Kalshi nowcasting probability estimation.

findings.title: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
findings.authors: Yijia Xiao, Edward Sun, Di Luo, Wei Wang
findings.venue: NeurIPS Multi-Agent AI Workshop (Oral), June 2025 update
findings.reason: Multi-agent framework with specialized analyst roles improves Sharpe and reduces drawdown vs single-agent baseline. Conceptually useful but too general to stage a concrete hypothesis now — would need a specific signal to test.

findings.title: FinRL-X: An AI-Native Modular Infrastructure for Quantitative Trading
findings.reason: Unified data→strategy→backtest→live framework succeeding FinRL. Architecturally interesting but our existing stack (yfinance + Vectorbt + Alpaca) already covers the same pipeline. No concrete signal advantage identified.

findings.title: Cointegration-based pairs trading with ETFs: stability and profitability (2000-2024)
findings.reason: Confirms cointegration pairs trading profitability depends heavily on cointegration stability and parameter choice, not specific pairs. Consistent with our H152-H160 NOT CONFIRMED results. No new actionable signal — confirms existing conclusion.

findings.title: Toward Expert Investment Teams: A Multi-Agent LLM System with Fine-Grained Trading Tasks
findings.reason: Fine-grained task decomposition in multi-agent LLM investment system improves risk-adjusted returns. Tested on Japanese equities. Interesting architecture but US equity application unclear without further investigation.

findings.title: Cross-sectional factor momentum: evidence from multiple formation periods
findings.reason: Confirms factor momentum with recent/intermediate formation periods. Our H001-H151 momentum research already covers this territory thoroughly. No new edge identified.

key_insights: Two high-value findings: (1) Press release NLP (arXiv:2509.24254) provides a second NLP channel for the PEAD pipeline that is additive to call transcript scoring — this is the most directly actionable finding given our live H163/H174 paper trading deployment. (2) PolySwarm's multi-LLM Bayesian aggregation (arXiv:2604.03888) directly addresses probability calibration quality in prediction market nowcasting — a known weakness in our current single-call approach. Both are staged as H184 and H185 respectively. The pairs trading and ETF cointegration literature continues to confirm our H152-H160 conclusions: the edge is thin and parameter-dependent. Multi-agent LLM trading frameworks are advancing rapidly but remain at the 'proof of concept' stage for production deployment.
